title: Hydrogen & its compounds
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: What is the difference between water and hydrogen peroxide?
How do we measure the hardness of water?
Can you explain what an isotope is with an example?

explain.say: Today we are learning about hydrogen and some of its compounds. We will look at isotopes and water.
An isotope means an atom of the same element. They have different numbers of neutrons. This changes the atom's mass.
Water is a compound made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. The formula is H two O.
Hydrogen peroxide is a different compound. It has two oxygen atoms and two hydrogen atoms. The formula is H two O two.
Water hardness is caused by dissolved mineral salts. These salts often contain calcium and magnesium ions. We measure this hardness.
In real life, you notice water hardness when you wash clothes. Hard water can leave soap residue on your laundry. This is due to the dissolved minerals.

draw.text: Real life: Soap scum on clothes

faq.q: What is the difference between water and hydrogen peroxide?
faq.a: Water is H two O, containing hydrogen and oxygen. Hydrogen peroxide is H two O two, meaning it has more oxygen atoms.
asks: What is the ratio of atoms in H₂O vs H₂O₂?
Can you compare the formulas for water and peroxide?

faq.a: Hard water contains dissolved minerals like calcium and magnesium. These minerals react with soap, making it difficult to wash clothes.
asks: Does the mineral content of water affect cleaning?

faq.q: Are isotopes the same as allotropes?
faq.a: No, isotopes are variations of an element with different neutrons. Allotropes are different structural forms of the same element, like carbon.
asks: Isotope vs allotrope, what is the difference?
Do isotopes change the chemical properties?

faq.q: How do we chemically remove water hardness?
faq.a: We often use chemicals like lime or soda ash to precipitate the calcium and magnesium ions out of the water. This process is called softening.
asks: What is the process of water softening?
What chemicals remove hardness from water?

faq.q: Does the number of protons determine the element?
faq.a: Yes, the number of protons defines the element. Changing the number of neutrons only creates an isotope of that same element.
asks: If I change neutrons, is it still the same element?

facts: Water has the chemical formula H two O.
Hydrogen peroxide has the chemical formula H two O two.
Water hardness is primarily due to dissolved calcium and magnesium ions.
Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

quiz.say: The formula for pure water is:
quiz.why: Water is chemically defined by two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

wrong.0: This formula suggests three oxygen atoms, which is incorrect for water.
wrong.2: This formula represents hydrogen peroxide, which has more oxygen.
wrong.3: This is missing one hydrogen atom, making it incorrect.

quiz.say: If an atom has 6 protons and 8 neutrons, what is its isotope?
quiz.why: Carbon has 6 protons, and adding 8 neutrons gives a mass number of 14.

wrong.0: This only accounts for the protons, ignoring the neutrons.
wrong.1: This changes the number of protons, making it a different element.
wrong.2: This only adds 2 neutrons, not the required 8 neutrons.

quiz.say: Which substance is most likely to cause soap scum in hard water?
quiz.why: These specific dissolved ions react with soap components in hard water.

wrong.0: Water itself is not the cause; it is the dissolved minerals in the water.
wrong.2: Oxygen gas is a gas and does not react with soap to form scum.
wrong.3: Hydrogen ions are related to acidity, not the primary cause of scum.
